chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musanna ibn Abd al-Salam, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
I asked him about the person in Ihram killing the bug and the flea when they intend (to attack) him. He said: Yes.

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا: One of the two Imams (referring to the 5th or 6th Imam)
key_terms.الْبَقَّة: The bug (specifically the bedbug or similar biting insect)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِم: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What insects can a person in Ihram kill if they bother them?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the prominent chain of Zurara from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), clarifies that the prohibition on killing specific animals during Ihram does not extend to small insects like bugs and fleas when they cause annoyance. It highlights the juristic principle of 'takhfif' (ease) in ritual purity, distinguishing between major fauna and minor pests that do not require expiation (kaffarah) upon being killed.
